messages:
julia-support: FYI customer ACME reported sudden p99 spikes on the tool-calling route (/v1/generate) since ~2026-03-16. p95 pretty stable (~120ms) but p99 jumped from ~600ms to ~2.8s. They said it affects endpoints with function-calling/structured_output enabled. Request id: `req_20260316_acme_09`

matt-ml: Can you paste a minimal repro request and the `tool_router` config they used? Also which model variant?

julia-support: sample payload below (sanitized):
```json
{
  "model": "redwood-13b-opt-v1",
  "tool_call": true,
  "tools": [
    {
      "name": "extract_entities",
      "schema": {"type":"object","properties":{"items":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"id":{"type":"string"},"attrs":{"type":"object","patternProperties":{"^.*$":{"type":"string"}}}}}}},"required":["items"]}
    }
  ]
}
```
They said enabling `validate_schema: true` in the router is required for their workflow. Seen in us-west and eu-west.

serena-runtime: I pulled traces for `req_20260316_acme_09`. Hotspot is JSON schema validation step — synchronous `jsonschema.validate()` in the tool router. CPU profile shows long tails in validator (single-threaded) and some blocking waiting on main event loop. Batches where structured output is enabled show 3x CPU time per token.

opsbot: alert: high-p99-toolcall-2026-03-16 triggered for svc=tool-router threshold=2000ms (count=18)

matt-ml: Ok. Likely two contributing factors: 1) heavy schema (patternProperties) => validator complexity, 2) validators being recompiled per-request or executed in main thread. Quick reproducer: curl to our hosted endpoint with same schema yields p99 ~2.6s on my dev box.

serena-runtime: Repro command (internal):
```bash
for i in {1..50}; do curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d @sample.json > /dev/null & done; wait
```
On canary we reproduced p99 ~2.5s. Flamegraph attached to ticket (INC-2026).

dana-eng-runtime: Mitigations to try (ordered):
1) Turn off `validate_schema` at router for impacted customers (config flag) -> immediate drop in CPU and p99.
2) Route to streaming responses so validation can be incremental or deferred to final chunk.
3) Cache compiled validators (checksum(schema) -> compiled validator instance) to avoid recompile.
4) Replace Python validator with faster Rust/Wasmer-based validator (benchmark shows 4-8x).
5) Short term: route ACME to lightweight model variant (redwood-13b-opt-warm) or dedicated capacity.

matt-ml: +1 for caching compiled validators and adding a schema complexity guard (reject schemas with patternProperties or deep nesting unless opt-in). Also add sampling: validate 1% of requests to detect regressions while offloading most traffic.

natalie-product: We need a customer update. If we plan to disable `validate_schema` as a temporary mitigation for them, can we offer a credit and ETA for a fix? Sales wants to avoid surprise.

julia-support: Created INC-2026, assigned to eng-runtime. Drafted message to ACME: "We're investigating increased p99 due to schema validation. Temporary option: disable server-side strict validation or enable a sampled validation mode while we optimize. We'll share ETA within 2 business hours." Waiting approval.

serena-runtime: Quick patch I tested on canary: we cache compiled validators keyed by schema SHA256 and use `fastjsonschema` (C-backed) instead of Python `jsonschema` when schema is simple (no patternProperties). Results: p99 dropped from 2.5s -> ~700ms on canary under same load. Patch diff: 
```yaml
router: 
  schema_validation: 
    enabled: true
    engine_priority: ["fastjsonschema","python-jsonschema"]
    cache_ttl_seconds: 3600
    sampling_rate: 0.01
```
```diff
- validator = jsonschema.Draft7Validator(schema)
+ key = sha256(schema)
+ validator = cache.get_or_create(key, compile_with_fastjsonschema(schema))
```

dana-eng-runtime: I'm deploying that to a 10% canary now. Also opening a follow-up to implement a runtime flag per-customer to disable validation.

opsbot: deploy: router-canary-2026.03.16-1250 -> success (10% traffic)

matt-ml: Monitoring tip: emit `validator_compile_ms` metric, `schema_size_bytes`, and `schema_complexity_score` so we can alert when validator time > X ms. Also add route-level `validation_backpressure` to fall back when validation queues exceed threshold.

julia-support: Can you confirm expected customer-facing message and timeline?

natalie-product: Proposed message: "We've identified schema validation as the cause of higher p99 for requests using structured output. We're rolling a performance fix to canary now and expect a reduction in p99 within the hour. Temporary options: disable server-side validation or opt into sampled validation. We'll follow up when patch hits your region." OK?

serena-runtime: Canary metrics after 12 minutes: p95 ~150ms, p99 ~720ms for validated traffic; overall p99 across canary down 65%. No errors introduced.

dana-eng-runtime: Plan: promote patch to 50% in 15min, monitor for regressions, then to 100% with a 1h soak. Also will add per-customer `validate_schema` flag so support can toggle per tenant.

julia-support: Sent message to ACME with mitigation options + credit offer. Ticket updated.

natalie-product: I'll coordinate credit and csf note. Please ping me if timeline slips.

matt-ml: Post-mortem action items: 1) Add compiled-validator cache + telemetry (owner: eng-runtime), 2) Implement schema complexity guard + opt-in for heavy constructs (owner: platform), 3) Docs: recommend lightweight schemas and client-side validation where possible (owner: devex).

julia-support: Closing loop: will update INC-2026 when patch promoted. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
